log:
incident-bot: Paging ops-oncall: ALERT: Elevated 429s and 5xx for org "mercuria" in us-west1 (from 03:12 UTC). Metric: org_rate_limited_requests spike +800% over baseline. Severity: high. Link: https://ops.metrics/redwood/mercuria

zack_ops: saw it, oncall taking

zack_ops: quick summary — customers hitting org RL hard, clients getting 429s and elevated latencies, starts ~03:10

carla_support: Mercruia SRE pinged support — they report user-facing failures for search and upload flows. Customer is on Dedicated (reserved) — says burst was from an internal data job

priya_sre: assigning to eng-sre to evaluate whether we can do a scoped RL override. Priya oncall rn

priya_sre: steps: 1) validate spike isn't abuse 2) if legit, apply temporary org-rl-bump via rl-service with TTL 3) monitor

riley_platform: +1. rl-service runbook: 
```
# temporary bump to allow org burst
rlctl patch --org mercuria --field rate_limit_per_minute=60000 --meta note="emergency-bump-03-12" --ttl 30m
```
We also have an API: POST /admin/orgs/{org}/rl/override {limit,expires,reason}

zack_ops: priya, can you confirm it's safe? Any downstream capacity risk on us-west1? We have spare headroom but need to avoid exhaustion

priya_sre: checked - cluster headroom ~28% for serving GPUs. Network egress within thresholds. Acceptable to apply a scoped bump for 30m

evan_am: I'm on the thread — notifying customer success and account execs. We need to log changes and require Mercuria to follow up with safer backoff in their job.

carla_support: sending note to mercuria: "We're applying a temporary rate allowance to prevent customer impact. Please pause the bulk job and open a ticket so we can advise on long-term throttling." — they acked

riley_platform: i'll prepare the command. tagging @automation-bot to run the override so ops doesn't have to do manual change

automation-bot: Running job: rlctl patch --org mercuria --field rate_limit_per_minute=60000 --meta "emergency-bump-03-12-by-zack" --ttl 30m

automation-bot: Job queued -> executor-3

metrics-bot: Note: Detecting change in 10s windows. Will post updated 429/latency graphs in 2m

priya_sre: while we do that, enable temporary prefix caching for mercuria's search route to reduce load: 
```
cachectl enable --org mercuria --route /api/search --ttl 60s
```

zack_ops: done. cachectl returned OK

automation-bot: Job executor-3: rlctl patch completed in 6.2s. New ephemeral limit applied: 60000/min, expires in 00:30:00. Change-id: ch_2026_5468012345

metrics-bot: Post-change snapshot (03:15 UTC): 429 rate for mercuria ↓ 93% vs peak, p95 latency ↓ 220ms

carla_support: Mercuria confirms user errors dropped and they can resume client activity with throttled backoffs. They request confirmation we'll revert after 30m

evan_am: I'll open a follow-up OKR with the customer for long-term guardrails. Also requesting a postmortem if they had no planned burst

priya_sre: created incident task INC-2467: "mercuria emergency rl bump" — includes timeline, change-id, owner @priya_sre

zack_ops: note: we should record cost impact estimate. riley, can you approximate added token/compute units from the bump window?

riley_platform: quick ballpark from traces: additional 18k requests served in 30m, est +$420 in infra run-rate. I'll add to the incident doc

priya_sre: also scheduling a rollback at 03:45 UTC. automation-bot will remove override. If we still see elevated errors after revert, we escalate to capacity

automation-bot: Scheduled job: revert rl override ch_2026_5468012345 at 03:45 UTC

metrics-bot: 03:31 UTC update: ongoing 429s minimal, error budget stable

zack_ops: thanks team. oncall handoff note: I'll include this in midpoint handoff to night oncall (maya)

maya_oncall: acknowledged, will watch the scheduled revert and take over monitoring

carla_support: logged customer-facing message and internal note. customersuccess notified.

automation-bot: Revert job executed at 03:45:12 UTC. Override ch_2026_5468012345 removed. Confirmed RL for mercuria back to baseline

metrics-bot: Post-revert snapshot (03:50 UTC): 429s remain low; no regression. p95 latency baseline restored

priya_sre: closing incident: short-lived org RL bump applied as emergency mitigation. Actions: (1) account exec follow-up with Mercuria for job backoff (Evan) (2) add automated pre-flight check for bulk jobs to flag exceedance (Priya/Riley) (3) cost reconciliation (Riley)

evan_am: I'll set the customer meeting.

zack_ops: thumbs for everyone :thumbsup:

carla_support: adding summary to INCIDENTS/mercuria/5468012345.txt and will trigger postmortem template

priya_sre: tagging for retro: we should consider an auto-approve flow if cluster headroom >25% and customer has good-faith SLA — reduces manual latency for future incidents

maya_oncall: noted. I'll pick that up in runbook updates

priya_sre: incident closed 03:55 UTC
